# Synthesis: watchlist and open questions

## The thesis in one paragraph

Cooling demand is one of the largest, most durable, climate-and-income-driven growth stories available, with the global AC stock projected to grow roughly 3.5× by 2050 [@iea2018cooling]. On top of that secular base sits a cyclical equipment business that is being *accelerated* by regulation — rising efficiency standards (SEER2) and the forced low-GWP refrigerant transition (AIM Act) — which raises selling prices, pulls forward replacement, and penalizes low-tech competitors [@doe2023seer2; @epa2024aim]. The investing task is to own that growth through companies where AC is a large, high-quality share of the business, at a price that doesn't already fully reflect it.

## Working watchlist

| Tier | Names (tickers) | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Core HVAC pure-plays** | Daikin (6367.T), Carrier (CARR), Trane (TT) | Largest, most AC-focused; levered to replacement + structural growth |
| **Concentrated US** | Lennox (LII) | Pure North American replacement + refrigerant cycle; best value/margins |
| **Europe heat-pump tilt** | NIBE (NIBE-B.ST), Carrier/Viessmann, Daikin, Mitsubishi (6503.T) | Direct exposure to European electrification runway |
| **Data-center cooling** | Vertiv (VRT), Modine (MOD), nVent (NVT) | AI-driven liquid-cooling demand; fastest growth, highest multiples |
| **Refrigerant chemicals** | Solstice (SOLS), Chemours (CC) | A2L/HFO transition; SOLS cleaner, CC higher torque + PFAS risk |
| **Components** | Sanhua (002050.SZ / 02050.HK); *Copeland IPO — watch* | Valve leader + EV-thermal crossover; Copeland IPO would add compressor access |
| **Diluted / context only** | Mitsubishi, LG, Samsung, JCI, Midea, Gree, Haier | Real AC exposure but inside larger groups or constrained-access listings |

: Working watchlist — a starting point, not a recommendation. {#tbl-watchlist}

## What would change the picture (risks)

- **Valuation.** The best businesses (Trane, Vertiv, Daikin's quality peers) rarely look cheap — quality and AI growth are at least partly priced in. Lennox and Daikin screen cheapest.
- **Antitrust overhang.** The 2026 HVAC price-fixing suits against Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Daikin and others put the "sticky ASP uplift" thesis at some risk; all defendants deny the claims, but it's unresolved. See the [regulation chapter](regulation-pricing.qmd).
- **AI-capex cyclicality.** The data-center cooling names (VRT/MOD/NVT) are levered to a concentrated set of hyperscaler customers and the AI capital cycle — high beta in both directions.
- **TFA / HFO regulation.** The refrigerant-chemicals thesis (SOLS/CC) carries a long-tail risk that HFOs themselves face future restriction as TFA scrutiny grows.
- **Cyclical air-pocket.** The 2024 pre-buy / 2025 shipment decline is near-term noise for a 10–15 year horizon, but could create a cheaper entry point worth exploiting.
- **China and tariffs; commodity low-end.** Volume leaders (Midea/Gree/Haier) and supply chains carry policy risk; window/portable units are commoditized — don't mistake volume leadership for profit leadership.
